findings.evidence: template/scripts/integration_contour.py:617-624 `requirement_checkpointed` catches RequirementRetrospectiveError, and RetrospectiveStale subclasses it, so stale returns False. Lines 765-766 then call `ensure_requirement_checkpoint`, which re-records the checkpoint over all events. `RetrospectiveStale` can therefore only escape from `reconcile_parent` (lines 957-960 of the diff) if friction arrives between those two calls. I read the diff and this file only and ran no tests. The tests in tests/test_autonomous_integration_contour.py may cover the path with a stubbed `reconcile_parent`.
findings.summary: The retrospective-refresh path may rarely fire. `run_terminal` already re-records the Requirement checkpoint whenever `requirement_checkpointed` is false, and that includes the stale case. I did not confirm whether `RetrospectiveStale` can still reach the keyed block other than through a race. I also did not confirm that the BR-987 scenario (friction recorded after the retrospective blocks terminal) actually exercises it.
